chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no harm in the fasting person undergoing cupping, except in the month of Ramadan, for I dislike that he be deceived with his life, unless he does not fear weakness for himself. Indeed, when we desired cupping in Ramadan, we underwent it at night, so it does not contradict the earlier reports, because the reason for the dislike in it is directed only toward one who fears weakness. As for one who does not fear that, there is no harm with him in any case.
ai.seo_question: Does cupping break the fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) nuanced ruling that cupping (*hijamah*) does not invalidate the fast, with the dislike (*karahah*) being conditional upon the fear of physical weakness rather than an inherent defect in the act itself. This view aligns with the practice of the Prophet and Imams who performed cupping at night in Ramadan, demonstrating that the precaution against deception (*gharar*) of the body’s strength is the primary scholarly concern, allowing for flexibility when the individual is confident in their endurance.
